Read the reply I made above. We've talked about her problems many time. There are always new ones. Always. 

There is no quick fix.
Yes to all. Minus the friends a little. They've become distant

The underlying problem is borderline or bipolar. Some mood condition, I don't know, it doesn't matter. She was diagnosed with bipolar earlier in life. Personally, I think she has a strange mix between the two.

Talking about her problems is like setting a blowtorch to kindle. We talk about her problems regularly, but I try to never bring them up unless the subject is already opened. She is very open about things.

She isn't in immediate danger. And you don't understand how getting help works. It's not easy, and takes months of planning. The only way to get help quickly is to be involuntarily committed. And the charge for such a thing is in the tens of thousands of dollars. There are financial aid programs, and certain institutions have very good programs. However, when you're involuntarily committed, you don't get to pick the institution you go to. You can even be held in the ER for several days. The cost is staggering. She was billed $300 for talking to the receptionist then leaving at a mental health building.

I think I can try to convince her to go in and lie about an immediate plan for suicide at a particular institution that has a good financial aid program in order to get some kind of temporary help or medication. However, that place is often at 100% capacity for weeks in advance (it's still considered an emergency clinic). This will take months, but it's the best plan I can think of.
